To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the fault pattern of the Mid- Atlantic Ridge near 37°N is dominated by a series of parallel faults, that there are no large transform offsets in this region, that the fault pattern is asymmetrical with respect to the median valley axis and that the fault pattern changes across the ridge axis.
the fault pattern of a spreading ridge near a fracture-zone is characterized by a series of parallel faults which trend approximately east-west.

the Mid-Atlantic ridge crest and median valley near 37 ° N is characterized by: a) a series of large-scale fault patterns, b) a large number of small-scale faults, c) a large number, and variety, of volcanic features, d) an abundance of sediment, e) a large number and variety of hydrothermal vents and f) an extensive area of sediment-covered, smooth, abyssal plain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the physical and chemical processes which control the distribution of the major and minor elements in the oceans and the atmosphere.
the study of the ocean floor in terms of its physical, chemical and biological properties.

the following: (1) the nature of the fault pattern and the relationship of this to the spreading process, (2) the nature of faulting and the relationship of faulting to the formation of the median valley.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the area of the Mid- Atlantic Ridge surveyed is a complex of fracture zones and ridge segments of different ages and that there is evidence for the existence of an older, inactive ridge segment, now buried under sediments and lava flows of the median valley, which is the source of the ridge crest and median valley topography of the area.
the fault pattern of a spreading ridge near a fracture zones is not as simple as it might seem at first sight, and that the fault pattern is not necessarily a simple function of the spreading rate.
the fault pattern of a spreading ridge near a fracture is a good indicator of the fault pattern.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sea floor is dominated by a series of parallel ridges and grooves.
the area surveyed was dominated by a complex pattern of fracture zone-related faults.
the area surveyed contains the most complex and varied fault pattern yet observed on the ocean floor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fault pattern is more complex and more variable than previously thought.
the Mid-Atlantic ridge is a great place to study plate tectonics, because of the abundance and accessibility of the data.
we have a better idea of what the seafloor looks like in the area of the 1973 survey, and how it has changed in the last 40 years.
